title: Signed integral line reduction and restriction data
statement: For a prime ell, finite extension E/Q_ell and scheme X, use the existing completed coefficient ring and its positive quotient rings [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every module sheaf L define its signed tensor powers, ordinary and completed derived line tensor functors, and the actual completion comparison. Define ordinary and derived reduction comparisons with their balancing, dual evaluation and strict quotient transition formulas. Define opposite-line evaluations, their normalization on K-flat flat-term representatives, and the ordinary/completed inverse equivalence predicates on the integral constructible full subcategory. These are exactly the existing definitions formerly in lem-pur-integral-line-reduction-restriction, moved to the shared data module. The power abbreviations now use the generic scalar tensor powers; power_eq_coefficient and finitePower_eq_coefficient prove object equality with the original constructions, including both signs and zero.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12 and Proposition 3.5.1 / Definition 3.5.2, pp. 22-24; generic signed-line specialization with finite reduction conditions

also.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to a quotient map on the same topos
Proof (3), last sentence interpreted in the derived-complete integral coefficient convention; extracted generic reduction/restriction argument

proof.text: Use the already constructed signed powers, scalar extension, derived tensor, K-flat representative comparisons and quotient completion. Record their existing pure-tensor formulas as predicates, and record restriction through the full integral subcategory by explicit functor isomorphisms and evaluation equations. No object is constructed from an arbitrary existence witness: the chosen tensor models are determined up to their compatible representative isomorphism. Induction on the natural exponent proves equality of the generic and coefficient positive powers; integer case analysis then proves power_eq_coefficient and finitePower_eq_coefficient, including internal duals.

proof_origin.place: Proof (3), the corresponding signed-line reduction/restriction steps; isolated from lem-pur-integral-line-reduction-restriction
